# Science Education Research

> > A comprehensive resource on science education research, featuring the work of Keith S. Taber from the University of Cambridge, covering student thinking, alternative conceptions, research methodology, and constructivist pedagogy.

This site provides academic resources, publications, and methodological guidance for researchers and educators in science education. It emphasizes learner cognition, conceptual change, and evidence-based teaching practices across chemistry, physics, and biology education.

## Key Topics

- alternative-conceptions
- student-misconceptions
- constructivism
- conceptual-understanding
- research-methodology

## Core Publications and Books

- [Student Thinking and Learning in Science](https://science-education-research.com/publications/books/student-thinking-and-learning-in-science): Keith Taber's Routledge book on learner ideas in science education
- [The Learner's Thinking](https://science-education-research.com/publications/books/modelling-learners-and-learning-in-science-education/the-learners-thinking): Springer book chapter on cognitive processing and metacognition in science

## Research Methodology

- [Grounded theory](https://science-education-research.com/research-methodology/grounded-theory): Overview of grounded theory methodology for qualitative research
- [Axial coding](https://science-education-research.com/research-methodology/analysis/axial-coding): Guide to axial coding and constant comparison in grounded theory analysis
- [The repertory grid technique](https://science-education-research.com/research-methodology/research-techniques/the-repertory-grid-technique): Kelly's repertory grid method based on Personal Construct Theory
- [Ethical reporting of educational research](https://science-education-research.com/research-methodology/research-ethics/ethical-reporting-of-educational-research): Guide to research ethics, anonymity, and authorship in education research
- [Observer role](https://science-education-research.com/research-methodology/research-techniques/observation/observer-role): Methods guide on participant observation and observer effects in research
- [Rhetorical research](https://science-education-research.com/research-methodology/research-design/rhetorical-research): Critique of weak research designs and rhetorical approaches in education

## Learning Theory and Cognition

- [Memory](https://science-education-research.com/learners-concepts-and-thinking/memory): Guide to memory, cognitive psychology, and learning theory concepts
- [Alternative Conceptions and the Learning of Chemistry](https://science-education-research.com/publications/papers/alternative-conceptions-and-the-learning-of-chemistry): Israel Journal paper on misconceptions and conceptual change in chemistry
- [Lost without trace or not brought to mind?](https://science-education-research.com/publications/papers/lost-without-trace-or-not-brought-to-mind): Longitudinal case study on memory and forgetting in chemistry education

## Pedagogy and Teaching Approaches

- [Constructivism – the good; the bad; and the abhorrent?](https://science-education-research.com/publications/miscellaneous/constructivism-good-bad-abhorrent): Seminar presentation on constructivism in educational theory & pedagogy
- [Constructivist pedagogy is superior](https://science-education-research.com/publications/miscellaneous/constructivist-pedagogy-is-superior): Debate on constructivist vs direct instruction in science education
- [Designing teaching activities to scaffold learning: understanding circular motion](https://science-education-research.com/publications/chapters/designing-teaching-activities-to-scaffold-learning-understanding-circular-motion): Chapter on scaffolding physics education for circular motion concepts
- [The risk to 'progressive' school science education under the influence of COVID-19](https://science-education-research.com/publications/miscellaneous/the-risk-to-progressive-school-science-education-under-the-influence-of-covid-19): COVID-19 impact on progressive pedagogy and formative assessment practices

## Student Misconceptions and Alternative Conceptions

- [A molecule is a bit of a particle – or vice versa](https://science-education-research.com/a-molecule-is-a-bit-of-a-particle-or-vice-versa): Student misconceptions about particle theory and atoms vs molecules
- [Is the theory of evolution e=mc²?](https://science-education-research.com/is-the-theory-of-evolution-emc%c2%b2): A-level student misconceptions about scientific theories and evolution
- [Are plants solid?](https://science-education-research.com/are-plants-solid): Student understanding of states of matter applied to plant biology
- [Student perceptions of the knowledge generated in some scientific fields](https://science-education-research.com/publications/articles/student-perceptions-of-the-knowledge-generated-in-some-scientific-fields): School Science Review article on student views of scientific knowledge

## Optional

- [An unpublished Theory of Everything](https://science-education-research.com/an-unpublished-theory-of-everything): Editorial perspective on peer review and unsolicited manuscript rejection
